Subject: ACME discovery recap + next steps

Hi Anne / Jake,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary: low-latency inference for chat assistants with reliable streaming.
- Secondary: function/tool calling + structured JSON outputs for downstream parsing.
- Scale: expect ~1k-2k concurrent end users initially, with peak bursts.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC/private deployment likely required for production.

Agreed next steps:
1) ACME to confirm which three workflows you want us to validate (suggest: 1) multi-turn chat with streaming responses and tool calls, 2) structured invoice parsing -> JSON, 3) high-concurrency throughput tests).
2) Redwood to provide a short POC test plan and baseline performance expectations (we will include recommended model variants and quantization options).
3) Schedule a 60-min POC kickoff w/ your infra & engineering.

I've attached the discovery notes and a short feature matrix comparing Redwood vs hyperscaler inference APIs (note: highlights below).

Redwood differentiators (brief):
- Streaming-first responses with robust function/tool calling semantics (designed to preserve structured outputs when streaming).
- Predictable latency under load via dedicated routing + autoscaling policies.
- Cost controls: batching + KV caching tuned per workload to reduce per-token unit cost.

Can you confirm the three workflows you want validated and availability for a kickoff next week (we have Tue/Wed afternoon PST open)?

Thanks,

Anne — perfect, thanks for confirming and for the schema. We've drafted a short test plan below and called out a few Redwood vs hyperscaler behaviors you'll likely see during evaluation.

Proposed POC test plan (high level):
A) Streaming + function calling (workflow):
  - Goal: validate partial-JSON streaming + immediate tool invocation for one critical path (search -> enrich -> respond).
  - Success criteria: downstream tool receives valid partial JSON in >= 95% of trials; end-to-end median latency < 250ms for token streaming segments in 90% of requests.
  - Tests: 1000 serialized requests, 5 sequential turns each (simulate chat).

B) Structured outputs (invoice schema):
  - Goal: ensure model returns schema-compliant JSON for nested objects/arrays.
  - Success criteria: schema validation pass rate >= 98% for top-level required fields; tolerance for optional fields documented.
  - Tests: 200 samples with typical / edge-case inputs.

C) Throughput & latency under concurrency:
  - Goal: observe p50/p95 latency and token cost across a 2k concurrent virtual user ramp.
  - Success criteria: p95 response latency <= 600ms for small responses; graceful degradation w/ autoscaling.

Redwood vs hyperscalers - what you'll see:
- Streaming fidelity: Redwood's runtime preserves structured output markers during streaming and supports function/tool call tokens mid-stream; some hyperscaler endpoints either buffer until completion or do not guarantee structured-delimited partial outputs.
- Predictable p95 under burst: our dedicated routing + KV caching reduces tail latency vs shared endpoints. Hyperscalers may show more variance at p95 under similar load.
- Cost tuning: Redwood can recommend quantized variants + batching that often reduce per-token cost with minor quality delta; hyperscalers generally expose fewer on-the-fly config levers for inference economics.

A couple logistics asks for the kickoff:
- Can your infra lead (we'll need an SRE/infra person) join the call?
- We'll need an initial dataset (200 invoice samples + a handful of chat prompts) uploaded to a shared S3/GDrive link before the kickoff.

Next: we will send a calendar invite for Wed Dec 09 10:00 AM PT and a short POC checklist. I'm cc'ing Laura from Solutions so she can scope the test harness.

Thanks,
--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
